name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: An AI assistant that can open up any app on your computer, binaries included, and explain exactly how a feature works so you can rebuild it yourself.
buyer: A product manager or indie founder at a small software shop who wants to copy a competitor's clever feature but has no source code and no reverse-engineering staff.
business_use_cases: A startup sees a slick onboarding animation in a competitor's desktop app and uses it to get a working explanation and a rebuildable version in an afternoon instead of guessing from a screen recording.
An agency that maintains old, undocumented internal Windows/Electron tools for clients uses it to figure out what a legacy app actually does before rewriting it.
A security consultancy uses the native-binary analysis to triage an unfamiliar executable a client found on their network, before deciding whether to escalate to a full malware investigation.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'competitive feature teardown' consulting service: clients send an app, you deliver a report and a buildable clone of one feature.
Package it as a paid add-on inside an existing dev-tools subscription aimed at agencies that inherit legacy codebases.

steal_this: Offer a $200 'tell me how that app feature works' report service for indie founders: they send a link or app, you run REA, and hand back the evidence plus a starter implementation.
